To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Russian human resource management system is in transition and is not ready for Western style management.

1) Russian HRM practices are based on a command-and-control approach, 2) Russian HRM systems do not have the flexibility to respond to changing business environments, 3) Russian HRM is not integrated with the overall business strategy, 4) Russian HRM has not been developed as a strategic business partner, and 5) Russian HRM does not provide the necessary support to managers.

the Russian HRM system, which was developed in the Soviet era and which has been retained in the post-Soviet period, is a system of centralized control and is incompatible with the Western system of HRM.

the following questions: (a) what is the state of the HRM function in Russian companies; (b) what are the major barriers to effective HRM; and (c) what are the implications for the future of HRM in Russia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Russian business culture has a long way to go to catch up with the Western world in the HRM arena.

the HRM problems are so pervasive and so deeply ingrained in the Russian business environment that the Western companies will have to be prepared to spend a great deal of time and money to make any progress in this arena.
Russian HRM is a work in progress, but that it is progressing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most significant barriers to successful HRM in Russia are the remnants of the Soviet era.
Western companies need to be more flexible in their approaches to Russian HRM and more willing to adapt to local conditions and practices.
Russian executives must be trained and coached to understand and appreciate the value and benefits of HRM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Western executives need to be aware of the historical and cultural context of Russian human resources and to be sensitive to the Russian mindsets and values.
Western executives need to be patient and flexible in dealing with Russian executives who, for the most part, have had little exposure to the Western business model.

the HRM problems are not so much in the area of the HRM systems and processes, as they are in the area of changing the mindsets of executives and managers who are responsible for the implementation of HRM systems.
